name: Menu
statusNote: comp.menu is the unchanged legacy flat dropdown; comp.standard-menu, comp.vibrant-menu and comp.segmented-menu are new Expressive grouped-item variants with rounded sub-container groups and corner-morphing.
summary: A temporary surface listing choices, opened from a button, icon or other anchor. The legacy flat dropdown is a plain list with an optional divider; Expressive menus compose the same items into rounded groups with a standard (surface-tinted) or vibrant (tertiary-tinted) container colour, with a segmented-menu geometry for grouped/selectable items.

inputs.name: expanded
inputs.description: Whether the popup is open. The caller owns it, normally bound to the anchor's toggle state.

inputs.name: onDismissRequest
inputs.description: Called when the user dismisses the menu, by pressing Escape or tapping outside it.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: The menu's items, optionally clustered into groups.

inputs.name: anchorPosition
inputs.description: Preferred side of the anchor to open toward; the menu falls back to the first candidate position that fits the window.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Colour treatment: legacy is the flat pre-Expressive dropdown; standard and vibrant are Expressive grouped menus differing only in container/item colour.

inputs.name: grouped
inputs.description: Clusters items into rounded segmented-menu sub-containers with corner-morphing instead of one flat list; composable with the standard or vibrant style.

inputs.name: selectedValue
inputs.description: The value of the currently selected item, for a menu used as a single- or multi-select control.

inputs.name: onItemSelected
inputs.description: Called with an item's value when the user chooses it.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The popup surface holding the item list, or a single group.

anatomy.name: Group
anatomy.description: Expressive only: a rounded sub-container clustering related items. A menu can hold one standalone group or several stacked leading/middle/trailing groups.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: A row: optional leading icon (swappable for a selected-state icon), label text, optional supporting text, optional trailing icon or trailing text such as a shortcut.

anatomy.name: Divider
anatomy.description: Legacy comp.menu only: separates item clusters in a flat list. There is no dedicated divider token; it is drawn with a generic HorizontalDivider.

anatomy.name: Group label
anatomy.description: Expressive only: optional heading text above a group's items.

anatomy.name: Focus indicator
anatomy.description: Ring drawn on the focused item or group.

variants.description: Plain flat list, one selected-item highlight colour; for pre-Expressive apps.
Expressive grouped menu, surface-tinted, low emphasis.
Expressive grouped menu, tertiary-tinted, high emphasis; use sparingly.
Items render as one undivided or divider-separated list.
Items render inside one or more rounded sub-container groups with corner-morphing on the group and its first/middle/last items; usable with the standard or vibrant style.

layout.text: Legacy item row minimum height is 48dp, minimum/maximum width is 112–280dp, and horizontal padding is 12dp.
The legacy popup's content gets 8dp of vertical padding and clips to the intrinsic maximum width of its items.

Expressive selectable item content padding is 12dp horizontal and 12dp vertical by default; an alternate 'precision pointer' sizing mode uses 16dp start / 10dp end instead. This is a hardcoded platform input-device toggle, not exposed as a token.
Group content padding is 0dp horizontal and 2dp vertical; minimum group height is 32dp.
The gap between stacked groups reads segmented-gap; the analogous gap for a horizontal icon-only row reads horizontal-icon-only-segmented-gap instead.

A segment's outer corner (the one facing away from neighbouring items) takes the larger item-first-child-shape or item-last-child-shape (both medium); the corner facing the adjacent item in the segment (the seam) takes the smaller item-first-child-inner-corner-corner-size (extra-small). This outer-vs-inner split is implied by the tokens but never stated directly by them.

The same outer/inner rule applies one level up to group shapes: a leading group gets sys.shape.corner.large on its outer (top) corners and sys.shape.corner.small on its inner (bottom) corners; a trailing group is the mirror. Only the middle group shape is a real token; the leading/trailing asymmetric corner pairs are hardcoded directly from sys.shape.corner.large/small and must be composed by the implementor.

The horizontal-* segmented-menu tokens (container/item spacing, icon-only item, active-container-shape) describe a horizontal icon-row segmented layout with no consuming code at the pinned commit; build this layout from the tokens alone, with no Compose reference implementation to cross-check.

No submenu/cascading-menu logic exists in Menu.kt at this pin; nested menus are user-composed by opening a second popup anchored to an item. Treat submenus as composing two menus, not a built-in feature.

states.text: The popup scales from 0.8 to 1.0 and fades from 0 to 1 alpha as it opens, and the reverse as it closes.
The popup's fade (as opposed to its scale) animates on fast-effects rather than fast-spatial.
Selection is shown by a shape morph from the unselected item shape to item-selected-shape (or the horizontal equivalent) plus the selected colour set.

A group's shape morphs from group-shape to inactive-container-shape only after it has been hovered at least once and hover then ends, tracked with a hasBeenHovered flag; the first render is never in the inactive shape.

Disabled items use opacity multipliers on label, leading and trailing content, with separate item-selected-disabled-* families for a disabled selected item; there is no colour blending, only plain alpha.

states.label: colour transitions
states.text: Container, text and icon colour transitions animate on fast-effects.

behaviour.text: The scale/fade pivot is a calculated transform origin derived from the overlap between the anchor and menu bounds; the menu grows from whichever corner or edge is closest to the anchor, not always a fixed corner.

Each anchor position (above/below/left/right/start/end) supplies an ordered list of x/y candidate positions, anchor-aligned first then window-edge-aligned; the first candidate that fits the window is used. There is no fixed pixel offset beyond the caller-supplied offset value.
The menu keeps a 48dp margin from the top and bottom edges of the window.
A leading selected icon, such as a checkmark, is optional caller content that cross-fades in and out via expand/shrink plus fade; there is no built-in checkmark glyph, the icon swap is opt-in.
Arrow keys move focus between items, Escape or an outside click dismisses the menu, and Enter or Space activates the focused item.

keyboard: Arrow keys move focus between items.
Escape dismisses the menu and returns focus to the anchor.
Enter or Space activates the focused item.
Clicking outside the menu dismisses it.
semantics: Items carry menuitem semantics; a checkable item reports the checkbox role instead.
A selectable item built with SelectableDropdownMenuItem reports the radio-button role, not the checkbox role used by a checkable item.
The screen reader announces the item label, its checked or selected state, and its disabled state.

notes.text: comp.segmented-menu.active-container-shape is typed as a raw dimension (24) in the token source rather than a shape reference; treat it as a corner-radius value, not a shape alias — it does not resolve to any sys.shape.corner.* step.
Standard vs vibrant is purely a colour swap between groupStandardContainerColor and groupVibrantContainerColor; pick one map application-wide per menu, don't mix within a single group.
The legacy comp.menu divider has no colour or spacing token of its own; reuse the app's generic divider token, with 12dp horizontal / 2dp vertical as the default gap.

Menu content width is intrinsic and clamped by the legacy min/max width constants; Expressive items don't carry that min/max width and instead let each item's shapes or group control geometry — don't apply the legacy 112–280dp clamp to Expressive items.

comp.vibrant-menu has no item-selected-disabled-container-color/opacity pair even though comp.standard-menu does; a disabled selected item in a vibrant menu must fall back to the enabled selected container colour at the disabled label/icon opacity rather than a dedicated disabled container token.
